name: University of Debrecen
summary: Debrecen university with 13 faculties, 8 campuses and 34,000+ students; English-taught degrees from medicine and engineering to music.

ib.text: No IB-specific rule or exam exemption is published: you sit Debrecen's own entrance exam or interview. English needs a B2 certificate from a proctored exam, or a medium-of-instruction certificate from your school.

programmes.name: Medicine
programmes.about: Six-year medical degree in English (360 ECTS) from the Faculty of Medicine, preparing doctors for specialist training and PhD study.
programmes.overview: The first two years cover foundation sciences such as anatomy, biochemistry and physiology, together with Hungarian language. Year three adds pathology, immunology and microbiology with introductory clinical subjects, year four brings surgery, internal medicine, pharmacology and radiology, and year five covers dermatology, neurology, psychiatry and family medicine, with thesis work. In the final year you care for patients in the departments of internal medicine, surgery, gynaecology, neurology, psychiatry and paediatrics. From the third year you also learn basic Hungarian to speak with patients. Graduates continue to specialist medical training or a PhD school.
programmes.ib: Entrance exam in biology plus chemistry or physics, written then oral; no IB exemption is published. A Basic Medicine Course year can be offered if you miss the mark.
programmes.selectionNote: Written test (45 min each) in biology and chemistry or physics, then an oral exam; results are admit, Basic Medicine Course, or reject. Medicine closed early for 2026.

programmes.name: Dentistry
programmes.about: Five-year dental degree in English (300 ECTS) balancing theory with intensive clinical practice; you also learn basic Hungarian to speak with patients.
programmes.overview: Year one covers biophysics, biostatistics, medical chemistry and oral anatomy, year two adds biochemistry, dental physiology and an introduction to prosthodontics, and year three brings clinical pathology, microbiology and propedeutics in restorative dentistry and oral surgery. In years four and five you work in complex dentistry, oral surgery, orthodontics, periodontology and paediatric dentistry, finishing with a thesis. Lab classes start in the first year, and manual techniques are developed through clinical training that balances theory with intensive practice.
programmes.ib: Entrance exam in biology plus chemistry or physics, written then oral; no IB exemption is published. Basic Hungarian is taught for patient contact.
programmes.selectionNote: Written and oral exam in biology and physics or chemistry, or completion of the Basic Medicine Course. The 2026/27 intake filled up and closed early.

programmes.name: Pharmacy
programmes.about: Five-year pharmacy degree in English (10 semesters) on the chemical, pharmaceutical and therapeutic properties of medicines and their use in practice.
programmes.overview: Year one covers general chemistry, mathematics, physics and biophysics, pharmaceutical biology, Latin and Hungarian. Years two and three introduce pharmaceutical chemistry, technology and analytical methods, and the last two years turn to clinical applications such as clinical pharmacology, clinical pharmacy and pharmacovigilance, with topics like radiopharmacy and pharmaceutical management along the way. Graduates work in public and hospital pharmacies, laboratories, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, government agencies and health maintenance organisations, and some continue to doctoral research.
programmes.ib: Entrance exam in biology plus chemistry or physics, written then oral; no IB exemption is published.
programmes.selectionNote: Written and oral entrance exam in biology and physics or chemistry, or completion of the Basic Medicine Course. 2027 deadline not published for this programme.

programmes.name: Nursing
programmes.about: Eight-semester nursing degree in English (240 ECTS), over half practical training, preparing you to care for people and communities at each level of health provision.
programmes.overview: Year one covers the general principles of healthcare and nursing, biophysics and imaging diagnostics, with anatomy, biochemistry, psychology, microbiology and pathology. Year two brings internal medicine, pharmacology, paediatrics and skills development, and year three covers psychiatry, surgery, neurology, gynaecology and obstetrics. In year four you study anaesthesiology and intensive care, emergency care and rehabilitation, and write a thesis. More than half the curriculum is practical training, including a long internship in healthcare facilities. Graduates work in hospitals, clinics, nursing homes and rehabilitation centres, and can continue to doctoral programmes.
programmes.ib: An entrance interview and a written biology exam; taught at the Nyíregyháza campus, not Debrecen. No IB exemption is published.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance interview on English, school studies, motivation and communication, plus a written biology exam. Taught in Nyíregyháza.

programmes.name: Physiotherapy
programmes.about: Eight-semester physiotherapy degree in English (240 ECTS) with strong clinical practice, training you to restore movement and quality of life.
programmes.overview: Year one covers anatomy, physiology, biomechanics and the basics of physiotherapy, including electro-, balneo-, hydro- and climatotherapy. Year two adds clinical propedeutics and applied training methods, with techniques such as mobilisation and manual therapy. In year three you study internal medicine, neurology and orthopaedics for physiotherapists and the physiotherapy of the movement system, and year four covers intensive therapy and rehabilitation, with clinical placements in neurology, orthopaedics and rheumatology and a thesis. A compulsory internship is built in. Graduates work in therapy and rehabilitation services, balneotherapy institutions, home care, private practice and prevention.
programmes.ib: An entrance interview on your English, school studies and motivation; no IB exemption is published.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance interview assessing your English, school studies, motivation and communication skills.

programmes.name: Public Health
programmes.about: Four-year degree in English (240 ECTS) training public health supervisors in the core concepts of public health and in proposing solutions to health problems.
programmes.overview: Year one covers cell biology, anatomy, physiology, biostatistics and an introduction to public health, followed by epidemiology, immunology, microbiology and environmental topics. The later years apply this to occupational health, child and adolescent health, health promotion and health policy. Field work and laboratory practice sit beside the theory, and an internship is part of the degree. Graduates work in public health agencies such as cancer registries, food safety authorities and screening programmes, in community development and international aid, or in the pharmaceutical industry and management consultancies.
programmes.ib: An entrance interview on your English, school studies and motivation; no IB exemption is published.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance interview assessing your English, school studies, motivation and communication skills.

programmes.name: Agricultural Engineering
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS incl. a 30-credit internship) on sustainable food production, balancing feeding a growing population with the environment.
programmes.overview: Year one covers zoology, agricultural botany and chemistry, mathematics, informatics, animal physiology, soil science and water management. Year two adds land use, agricultural machinery, crop production, agroecology, animal husbandry and horticulture, and year three covers plant genetics and breeding, animal health, food technologies, quality management, farm business, forestry and integrated plant protection. The final semester is a twelve-week professional internship plus thesis work. Graduates work in agricultural enterprises, including management, in advisory and administration, in research institutes, on their own farms and in advocacy organisations.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and either chemistry or biology; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and chemistry or biology; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Biochemical Engineering
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS with internship) combining theory and engineering practice across biotechnology.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics, physics, general and organic chemistry, cell biology, microbiology and mechanical engineering. Year two moves into biochemistry, molecular biology methods, unit operations, bioprocess engineering, microbial physiology and genetics, and year three adds bioinformatics, analytical chemistry, plant biochemistry and spectroscopy. The last year covers quality management, safety and a thesis. A six-week placement at a company or research institute is part of the degree. Graduates can choose among careers across biotechnology, in research and development or in more practical roles.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and either chemistry or biology; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and chemistry or biology; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Chemical Engineering
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS) in chemical engineering with technology, safety, environmental protection, management and social-science content.
programmes.overview: After mathematics, physics, general, inorganic and organic chemistry in year one, you study physical and colloid chemistry, unit operations, process control, macromolecular chemistry and chemical technology. Year three adds qualitative and quantitative analysis, instrumental methods, plastics and processing, computer modelling of chemical technology systems, environmental technology and pilot plant work. Hands-on laboratory courses run alongside the theory, with a six-week internship at a company or research institute, and the last year covers safety and a thesis. Graduates can go on to master's programmes in chemistry, chemical, materials, environmental or bioengineering, or to a PhD in chemistry.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and chemistry; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and chemistry; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Civil Engineering
programmes.about: Eight-semester degree in English (240 ECTS) preparing you for planning, design, management and construction work in the public and private sector.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics, physics, technical drawing, CAD modelling, mechanics, hydraulics, construction materials and geoinformatics. Year two adds hydrology, geology, geotechnics, transportation engineering and GIS, and year three covers water management, building construction, construction management, reinforced concrete, steel, timber and masonry structures and finite element modelling. The last year includes bridge design and a thesis project, and a six-week placement at a company or research institute is part of the degree. Graduates work as design, structural, building services and consulting or contracting civil engineers, construction managers and building control surveyors, or move into business and finance.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Electrical Engineering
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS) in electrical engineering, adding project planning, problem-solving and management skills.
programmes.overview: You start with mathematics, physics, materials science, programming, electricity, measurements and electronics, then move to digital electronics, microelectronics, LabVIEW programming, circuit simulation and automation. Year three covers electronic technology, telecommunication, electric power systems and production management, and the last year adds enterprise economics and a thesis. A summer practice at an external professional institution is included. Graduates design, develop and maintain electrical control systems and components in engineering consultancies, manufacturing, automotive and railway engineering, steel manufacturing and water companies, working in multidisciplinary project teams.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Engineering Management
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS incl. internship) bridging engineering and business management: financial, human and production processes.
programmes.overview: The first years combine engineering foundations (mathematics, physics, mechanics, materials, electronics) with economics, accounting, quality management, project management, lean management, finance and law. In year three you choose one of three tracks: Construction, Industrial Process Engineering, or Material Handling and Logistics. A compulsory six-week practice and a thesis finish the degree. Graduates work as project, operations, supply chain, engineering and production managers, and can continue to a master's.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Environmental Engineering
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS) on protecting the environment: sustainable resource use, energy efficiency, pollution control and waste management.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics, chemistry, applied biology, ecology and engineering informatics. Later years bring environmental techniques, noise control, waste management, air quality, soil management and monitoring, then environmental law, radiation protection, water environment protection, impact assessment and GIS, and finally environmental economics, project management and complex planning. A compulsory six-week internship at a company is included, and the thesis spans the last two years. Graduates work in industry on sustainable practice, emissions and waste, in government on environmental policy and regulation, and in research and consultancy on environmental technologies and impact assessments.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and chemistry or physics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and chemistry or physics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS) in designing, operating and maintaining mechanical systems, with tracks in automotive production, building services or operation and maintenance.
programmes.overview: The first year covers mathematics, engineering physics, statics, materials engineering, technical drawing and CAD, and the second adds strength of materials, thermodynamics, dynamics and vibration, machine elements, measurement technology and fluid mechanics. In the second half you choose a track: Automotive Production Process Control, Building Services Engineering, or Operation and Maintenance. A compulsory six-week practice at a production company is included, along with a thesis. Graduates work in the automotive, chemicals, construction, metals, oil and gas, power generation, rail and utilities industries.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; English at B2 is also required. Choose one of three specialisation tracks.

programmes.name: Mechatronics Engineering
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS) combining mechanical engineering with electronics, electrotechnics and computer control.
programmes.overview: You study mathematics, engineering physics, electromagnetism, electronics and materials engineering, then mechanical machines, manufacturing technologies, mechatronic devices, measurement and data acquisition, pneumatics and hydraulics. Later subjects include electropneumatics, robots and robotic technology, electrical machines and drives, thermodynamic processes and cyber-physical systems, ending in a mechatronics project and thesis. Practical training runs throughout, with a compulsory six-week practice at a production company. Graduates work in robotics, automation, aircraft engineering, biomedical systems, transport and computer-aided design.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Vehicle Engineering
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS) on designing, manufacturing and repairing automotive, railway, naval and aircraft systems and machinery.
programmes.overview: The programme covers design and manufacturing, control systems and modelling, with significant emphasis on practical training and a compulsory six-week professional practice. In the latter half you choose a track: Vehicle Manufacturing, Automotive Vehicle Engineering, or Aircraft Engineering. A thesis completes the degree. Graduates work across transportation and manufacturing in the design, production and maintenance of automotive, railway, naval and aircraft systems, in mobile machinery, construction equipment and power management, and can continue to a master's.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Business Administration and Management
programmes.about: Seven-semester business degree in English (210 ECTS incl. internship): analysing, planning, organising and managing business organisations, with a chosen specialisation.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics, business informatics, economics, finance, communication, financial accounting, organisational behaviour and business law, followed by macroeconomics, corporate finance, marketing, international economics and statistics. Year three adds human resource management, controlling, EU studies, project management, entrepreneurship, decision theory and international business. The final semester is a mandatory internship and the thesis. Graduates work as human resources officers, marketing and sales executives, logistics and distribution managers and similar roles, and can move on to a master's.
programmes.ib: Entrance exam in mathematics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exam in mathematics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Commerce and Marketing
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS incl. internship) blending economic theory with practical marketing and commerce insight.
programmes.overview: Year one covers economics, marketing basics, accounting, business law, EU studies and statistics, then management, corporate finance, marketing research, foreign trade and business planning. Year three adds enterprise resource planning systems, trade economics, brand management, pricing, services marketing, marketing channels, international marketing and advertising. A semester-long practice at a multinational or local company or non-profit organisation and a thesis close the degree. Graduates work in advertising, public relations, account and brand management, marketing and sales, and can continue to a master's and later a PhD.
programmes.ib: Entrance exam in mathematics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exam in mathematics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Business Informatics
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS) training people who link business software developers and users, with business IT certification possible.
programmes.overview: The degree combines business and IT: management, business law, microeconomics and accounting alongside programming, operating systems and data management in year one. Year two adds finance, marketing, databases and business intelligence in practice, and year three covers software development and testing, SAP training, big data analytics and data visualisation. The last year includes data security, digital marketing and the foundations of artificial intelligence. An eight-week internship, at the university on research projects or at a company, and a thesis complete it. Graduates work as business analysts, system administrators and business data system developers.
programmes.ib: Written and oral entrance exam in mathematics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Written and oral entrance exam in mathematics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: Six-semester degree in English (180 ECTS) on designing, building and maintaining software-oriented IT systems, with a mandatory internship.
programmes.overview: Year one covers discrete mathematics, programming, operating systems, calculus, databases, data structures and algorithms and cloud computing. Year two adds high-level programming languages, web technologies, applied statistics, software engineering and the foundations of artificial intelligence, with machine learning, image processing and game development. Year three covers web application development, software testing and data security, and a thesis. You apply the theory in an eight-week internship at the university on research projects or at a company. Graduates usually start as junior software developers, building mobile, desktop, web and multimedia applications, and can continue to a master's.
programmes.ib: Written and oral entrance exam in mathematics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Written and oral entrance exam in mathematics; English at B2 is also required.

separateFrom.name: Computer Science Engineering
separateFrom.reason: Different degree: adds an engineering approach and maths plus physics exams, seven semesters.

programmes.name: Computer Science Engineering
programmes.about: Seven-semester degree in English (210 ECTS): informatics with an engineering approach, for implementing and running information and technical systems.
programmes.overview: Year one covers programming, electronics, physics, calculus, data structures, digital design and computer architectures. Year two adds networks, operating systems, control systems, software development, enterprise systems, web solutions and microcontrollers, and year three covers artificial intelligence, embedded systems, databases, IT security, computer graphics and telecommunication systems. The last year includes sensors and actuators and a thesis, and an eight-week internship at the university or a company is required. Graduates work as system designers, programmers, software and database developers, web designers and system administrators in production, services, banking, commerce and the civil service.
programmes.ib: English test and oral exam, plus maths and physics exams; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: English placement test and oral exam, plus written and oral exams in mathematics and physics.

separateFrom.name: Computer Science
separateFrom.reason: Different degree: six semesters with a maths exam only, without the engineering approach.

programmes.name: Biology
programmes.about: Six-semester degree in English (180 ECTS) on running experimental procedures and biological monitoring, with biochemistry, cytology and genetics.
programmes.overview: Year one covers biological chemistry, the fundamentals of biology, plant and animal taxonomy, microbiology and ecology. Year two adds cell biology, plant and animal physiology, genetics, molecular biology and bioinformatics, and year three covers human biology, evolutionary biology, population genetics and a thesis. Hands-on experience is built in, including a six-week practice at a company or research institute. Graduates can continue to master's programmes in molecular biology, biology, bioengineering or environmental science, or work in research laboratories, schools, hospitals, environmental agencies and pharmaceutical, food, agricultural and chemical companies.
programmes.ib: Written and oral entrance exam in mathematics and biology; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Written and oral entrance exam in mathematics and biology; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Biotechnology
programmes.about: Three-year degree in English (180 ECTS) applying biology to industrial, agricultural and biomedical problems.
programmes.overview: Year one covers physics, general, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry, mathematics, cell biology, microbiology and genetics, with courses in communication and bioethics. Year two adds analytical chemistry, biophysics, bioinformatics, biochemistry, immunology, molecular biology and industrial and environmental biotechnology, and year three covers systems biology, bioanalytics, synthetic biology and pharmaceutical, medical, agricultural and food biotechnology, plus a thesis. Laboratory work runs throughout, with a six-week internship at a company or research institute. Graduates work in pharmaceutical, food, agricultural and chemical companies, research institutes and hospitals, or continue to a master's.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in biology and chemistry; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in biology and chemistry; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Chemistry
programmes.about: Six-semester degree in English (180 ECTS) training chemists in theory and practice, grounded in maths, physics, informatics and biology.
programmes.overview: Year one combines mathematics, physics, general, inorganic and organic chemistry, environmental science, chemical informatics, nuclear chemistry and a physical chemistry laboratory. Year two covers analytical and physical chemistry, separation techniques, spectroscopy, colloid chemistry and chemical technology, and year three adds quality management, biochemistry, environmental chemistry and technology, visits to chemical companies and a thesis. A six-week practice at a company or research institute is included. Graduates can take up entry-level jobs as chemists, clinical laboratory technologists or materials scientists, or continue to a master's in chemistry, chemical engineering or molecular biology.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in chemistry and mathematics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in chemistry and mathematics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Earth Sciences
programmes.about: Six-semester degree in English (180 ECTS) on the planet's deep processes and the evolution of its surface environments.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics, physics, mineralogy and geology, biology, chemistry, historical geology, physical geography, soil geography and ecology, along with earth sciences fieldwork. Year two adds structural geology, cartography, biogeography, hydrology, hydrogeology and climate studies, and year three covers geothermics, surface analyses and a thesis. You also complete a short practice at an external company, institution, university or research laboratory. Graduates work in environmental protection, resource management and geological surveying, or continue to a master's.
programmes.ib: Written and oral entrance exam in geography and mathematics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Written and oral entrance exam in geography and mathematics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Mathematics
programmes.about: Six-semester degree in English (180 ECTS) joining algebra, analysis and geometry to applications in computer science and physics.
programmes.overview: Year one builds the basics: algebra and numbers, linear algebra, combinatorics and graph theory, geometry and analysis. Year two adds advanced algebra, number theory, multivariable calculus, computational geometry, linear programming, measure theory and numerical analysis, and year three covers differential equations, differential geometry, probability theory, cryptography, economic mathematics, optimisation and statistics, with a thesis. The programme balances theory with applications in computer science and physics. Graduates can work in government, teaching or industry, or continue to a master's in mathematics, applied mathematics or software engineering.
programmes.ib: Written and oral entrance exam in mathematics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Written and oral entrance exam in mathematics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Physics
programmes.about: Six-semester degree in English (180 ECTS) linking natural laws to experimental research: measurement, data evaluation and laboratory work.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics for physics, mechanics, thermodynamics, optics, calculus and linear algebra, with laboratory practicals alongside. Year two adds electromagnetism, condensed matter, quantum physics, differential equations and statistics, and year three covers quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, statistical physics, fundamental interactions and a thesis project. A six-week practice at an external company or institution is required. Graduates work in quality assurance, environmental protection and materials science, or move on to postgraduate study in physics, chemistry, biology, engineering, informatics or economics.
programmes.ib: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance exams in mathematics and physics; English at B2 is also required.

programmes.name: Communication and Media Studies
programmes.about: Six-semester degree in English (180 ECTS) on the theory and analysis of how information works in society, with practical media production.
programmes.overview: You study communication and media theory, media culture, film industry, scriptwriting, media law, ethics and economics in year one, then media text analysis, a media lab, strategic communication and marketing, and later press and media relations, news editing, press photography, radio and television studio training and creative writing. A journalism track is available, a 120-hour internship in editorial or corporate settings runs in the fifth semester, and a thesis completes the degree. Graduates work as journalists and broadcasters, in audiovisual content creation, public relations and social media management.
programmes.ib: An English placement test and an oral entrance exam; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: English placement test and an oral entrance exam; B2 English is required.

programmes.name: English and American Studies
programmes.about: Six-semester BA in English (180 ECTS) on advanced English plus the cultures, literatures and histories of English-speaking countries.
programmes.overview: Year one builds language skills in reading, writing, speaking and listening, with grammar, pronunciation and British and American civilisation. Year two adds applied linguistics, American and British literature and culture, visual culture and the history of the USA and the British Isles. After the first year you choose a four-semester specialisation, then a two-semester track in year three, among Business English, English-Hungarian Translation, a minor in another programme, British Literature and Culture, Linguistics and Communication, and North American Studies. Graduates work in business and government, media, publishing, tourism and diplomacy, or continue to an English Studies or American Studies master's.
programmes.ib: An entrance interview on your English, school studies and motivation; no IB exemption is published.
programmes.selectionNote: Entrance interview assessing your level of English, high school studies, motivation and communication skills.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.about: Six-semester degree in English (180 ECTS) covering developmental and social psychology and applied branches, with measurement and intervention techniques.
programmes.overview: Year one covers the history of philosophy, communication theory, biology basics, statistics, and experimental, developmental, personality and social psychology. Year two adds research methodology, evolutionary psychology, personality diagnostics, sport, work and clinical child psychology, and year three has individual research projects, psychophysiology, psycholinguistics, helping relations, clinical and health psychology and a thesis. Graduates work as human behaviour analysts in recruitment, education and health organisations, assisting school or organisational psychologists or laboratory researchers under the supervision of a qualified psychologist, and the degree is a base for any psychology master's.
programmes.ib: English placement test, oral exam and online multiple-choice test; no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: English placement test and oral exam, plus an online multiple-choice test; B2 English is required.

programmes.name: Classical Performing Arts (Music)
programmes.about: Six-semester music BA in English (180 ECTS) developing performing skills and theory, with some 20 instrument, singing and conducting specialisations.
programmes.overview: You study technique and performance in your chosen instrument, voice or conducting, alongside music history and theory, solfege, folk music, acoustics, philosophy, art history, repertoire studies, piano, methodology and stage practice. Orchestra or choir, chamber music and ensemble work balance theory with practice, and an internship is part of the curriculum. You can specialise in piano, organ, guitar, strings, recorder, woodwind, brass, percussion, singing or choral conducting. Graduates work in musical institutions, professional ensembles and roles that need music education, or continue to a master's specialisation.
programmes.ib: A programme-specific entrance exam (music); no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Programme-specific entrance exam, in music; specialisations run from piano, organ and strings to singing and choral conducting.

programmes.name: Contemporary Music
programmes.about: Six-semester BA in English (180 ECTS) taking one specialised instrument, contemporary vocals and music theory, aimed at the modern music industry.
programmes.overview: The curriculum covers the history of classical and popular music, folk music and arrangements, solfege, music theory and applied composition, with cultural history, philosophy, improvisation, orchestration and sound editing. It is rich in hands-on experience and teaches practical artistic methods and professional performance tools. You choose an instrument from piano, organ, guitar, strings, recorder, woodwind, brass or percussion, or choose singing or choral conducting. Graduates work in musical institutions, professional ensembles and roles that need music education, or continue to a master's specialisation.
programmes.ib: English placement test, oral exam and an online multiple-choice test; no IB exemption is published. B2 English required.
programmes.selectionNote: English placement test with oral exam, and an online multiple-choice test; B2 English is required.

programmes.name: Musical Creative Art and Musicology
programmes.about: Six-semester music BA in English (180 ECTS) in creative musical art and musicology, entered through a programme-specific music entrance exam.
programmes.overview: Music theory and solfege are the main subjects, supported by music history, folk music, philosophy, art history, acoustics, repertoire studies, choral conducting, transposing and score reading, composition, choir, piano and voice, with a thesis. The curriculum balances theoretical depth with practical knowledge and performing skills. Graduates work as music theoreticians or music assistants in music institutions and other jobs that need music education, helping to spread Hungarian and European music culture, and can continue to a master's specialisation.
programmes.ib: A programme-specific entrance exam (music); no IB exemption is published. English: B2 certificate, or a school medium-of-instruction certificate.
programmes.selectionNote: Programme-specific entrance exam, in music; B2 English is also required.

notes: Medicine and Dentistry stopped taking 2026 applications early because of high demand, so apply as soon as the 2027 window opens.
Prices are published in US dollars per year for all applicants, with no separate EU rate; the application fee is USD 150 and the entrance exam fee USD 350.
The university counts 36 English bachelor's degrees but its programme pages cover the 33 listed here; ask the admissions office about Food Engineering, Geography and Kindergarten Education.
